messages:
alex: :rotating_light: Observed sudden p99 spike on router ingress for eu-west-2; streaming requests showing stalls and a backlog of long polls. p95 ~ 0.9s, p99 ~ 12.4s, error rate still low but customers seeing stall behaviour. root ts 3633333333
incident-bot: Incident triggered: latency_slo_breach - router_ingress_euw2 (p99 > 10s). Paginating on-call. Pager sent to @maya.
pagerbot: Paging maya (on-call). Full incident channel: #incidents. Join when able.
maya: on it, joining bridge now. Can someone paste a quick graph/time series for router tail and LB queue depth?
alex: attaching quick snapshot (from the chat):
```
metrics: router_ingress.p99 (eu-west-2)
- 10:02:00 -> 3.1s
- 10:03:00 -> 4.2s
- 10:04:00 -> 8.9s
- 10:05:00 -> 12.4s
LB queue depth: backend-lb-euw2.queue_len -> spike from 200 -> 2.4k
streaming stalls: alive-streams waiting > 30s increased x6
```
sam: looks like routing skew, hot partitioning. I see a recent routing-policy deploy 10:00 that changed shard affinity seeds. Might be causing hotshard concentration.
lindsey: confirmed, rollout trace shows "rb-routing-v2" pushed to euw2 at 09:59 with new sticky-hash logic.
maya: plan: 1) reduce client-side affinity by disabling sticky-hash in euw2 2) enable temporary smoothing (hash_smoothing=true) 3) drain overloaded backends with weight adjustments 4) monitor p99 for 15m.
alex: +1. Any quick mitigation command?
sam: run this to flip the policy to fallback mode (10m):
```
# infractl is our routing config tool
infractl set-routing --zone eu-west-2 --policy rb-routing-v2 --override-mode fallback --ttl 600
infractl set-routing --zone eu-west-2 --sticky-affinity off --ttl 600
```
lindsey: executing override now (running infractl). will coordinate with oncall and ops to avoid cascading.
incident-bot: Deployment override applied by lindsey at 10:06:12 (3633333972). Mode: fallback TTL 600s.
maya: also queuing a per-node weight reduction for the three hottest pools to spread traffic:
```
rbctl adjust-weight --pool gpux-23 --zone eu-west-2 --delta -0.45
rbctl adjust-weight --pool gpux-19 --zone eu-west-2 --delta -0.30
rbctl adjust-weight --pool gpux-07 --zone eu-west-2 --delta -0.25
```
alex: Ran the first two adjustments; third still queued. Observed immediate drop in LB queue length by ~40% in first 30s.
sam: note: streaming sessions are sticky at the app layer; we can evict sessions older than 60s to free KV cache and reduce tail. Run this if p99 stays > 10s after 2m.
maya: adding that to plan as step 2b.
10:07:30 - maya: p99 down to 6.0s, p95 0.8s. queues trending down.
10:08:15 - alex: customers reporting reduced stalls but 2 large customers still seeing >8s tail in streaming. Pulling request logs for those accounts.
sam: found hot key patterns from two customers: extremely long-lived streams with large prefixes causing one shard to do heavy KV lookups. Suggest temporary per-tenant rate cap for long poll reopens.
lindsey: applied tenant cap rule for tenant-IDs: T-9834, T-7721 (10rps cap for new streams) via rate-policy service.
10:10:02 - incident-bot: Alert suppressed: router_ingress.p99 trending down. Keep monitoring for 30m.
maya: customer impact summary (initial): - window 10:03-10:10 UTC - p99 breach for eu-west-2 - ~0.12% requests > 10s, streaming stalls increased by ~6x - Affected: multiple internal routes; two enterprise tenants saw user-facing interruptions (support ticket inflow increasing).
alex: mitigation timeline recap: 10:06 infractl fallback override -> immediate queue relief. 10:07 weight adjustments -> further smoothing. 10:08 tenant caps -> removed hottest tail sources.
sam: root cause hypothesis: policy change (rb-routing-v2) introduced overly aggressive sticky-hash behavior combined with a small set of heavy streaming sessions; this amplified hot partitioning and overloaded LB queues causing tail stalls and some streaming timeouts.
maya: next actions: - revert sticky-hash rollout (permanent rollback) - add canary testing for routing seed changes - create smaller rolling window for sticky-affinity flips - postmortem owner: sam - ETA for rollback and follow-up: 3h for full rollback verification and postmortem draft in 24h.
lindsey: starting rollback now to rb-routing-v1. Command: `infractl set-routing --zone eu-west-2 --policy rb-routing-v1 --force`
incident-bot: Rollback initiated by lindsey at 10:12:55. Auto-notify on completion.
10:14:40 - alex: p99 now 1.9s, p95 0.45s, queues back to baseline ~180. Streaming stalls down to normal.
maya: good containment. Opening incident bridge for 30 more minutes to watch. Sam please gather the config diff and trace spans for the postmortem.
sam: will collect traces and push to /incidents/3633333333/artifacts by EOD. Will also propose a mitigations doc: avoid sticky-affinity flips during peak traffic windows, run synthetic hotkey tests, and add canary hashing.
alex: notifying support and account teams for the two affected tenants with a short RCA and interim mitigation notes.
10:30:00 - incident-bot: Incident resolved -> severity lowered to SEV2; monitoring continue.
maya: closing the active mitigation loop; will keep channel open for updates. Thanks everyone. :heart_pulse:
